editorialRulesApplied: Lived moments illustrate the transit; one invented scenario does not carry the whole card.
The close lands inside the consequence rather than assigning a task.
Cycle facts are removed from prose and supplied as an engine-rendered fact line under the date range.

articles.engineRenderedFactLine: Mercury moves through all twelve signs in about a year and usually spends roughly two weeks to two months in each sign. A retrograde can extend one stay.

article.opening: Mercury enters Gemini on {{entryDate}}, and one question becomes five before the first answer is finished. The original source gets found. A contradiction appears. The group chat fills with links, screenshots, and a version of the story that changes every ten minutes.
article.tension: Mercury in Gemini moves quickly because every answer opens another route. That speed can find the missing fact, connect two ideas, or give a stuck conversation somewhere new to go. It can also outrun the point. More tabs open, side questions take over, and the quickest summary gets repeated while the slower source that contradicts it goes unread. The conversation stays lively after it has stopped helping.
article.development: The cost shows up when a choice has to be made and nobody can tell which version is current. The confirmed detail is buried under commentary. The original question has been replaced by all the interesting questions that came after it. Curiosity found more information and lost the answer it was looking for.
article.close: By {{exitDate}}, the useful answer may be the one we almost missed while proving how much else we could find.
try_this: We can read the original source before repeating the quickest summary.
We can answer the question that was asked before adding another one.
We can let one interesting link wait until the decision in front of us is made.

article.opening: Mercury enters Virgo on {{entryDate}}, and the sentence that almost went out wrong gets caught in time. A number does not match. Two messages describe the same decision differently. Someone notices before the mistake becomes the version everyone remembers.
article.tension: Mercury in Virgo is good at finding what needs to be corrected. The trouble begins when every detail starts to feel equally dangerous. A clear answer gets checked for tone, then punctuation, then every possible exception. Everyone is still waiting while the useful reply becomes a perfect reply that arrives too late.
article.development: A mistake that changes the meaning deserves attention. A sentence that could simply be prettier does not carry the same risk. When that difference disappears, precision becomes a way to avoid being wrong in public. The extra checking creates the confusion it was supposed to prevent.
article.close: Before {{exitDate}}, the late answer may cause more confusion than the imperfect one ever would.
try_this: We can compare the two messages and mark the detail that changes the decision.
We can ask the factual question underneath one recurring worry.
We can leave a harmless wording preference alone when the meaning is already clear.

articles.engineRenderedFactLine: Mars moves through all twelve signs in about two years and usually spends roughly six to seven weeks in each sign. A retrograde can extend one stay.

article.opening: Mars enters Aries on {{entryDate}}, and waiting starts to feel worse than whatever happens next. The call gets made. The answer gets demanded. The part everyone has been circling finally has a name.
article.tension: The problem is that relief can look a lot like certainty. Once the pressure breaks, every delay feels personal and every objection feels like something to defeat. We answer before we know what was actually said. We fix the first problem we can reach, even when it is not the one causing the damage.
article.development: Mars in Aries is good at beginning. It is less interested in cleaning up what happened because nobody stopped long enough to decide what they were trying to change.
article.close: Before {{exitDate}}, notice which fight is moving the situation forward and which one is only giving the anger somewhere to go.
try_this: We can make the call and ask the direct question before explaining our position.
We can stop a rushed fix when it becomes clear that it is solving the wrong problem.

article.opening: Mars enters Scorpio on {{entryDate}}, and the question nobody wanted to answer becomes the only one that matters. The story changes. A promise no longer matches what happened. Silence that once bought time starts to look like a decision.
article.tension: Mars in Scorpio can stay with what others avoid. That is its strength. It becomes a problem when staying turns into watching, testing, and waiting for the next betrayal. We reread every response, hold back what we know, and ask the same question in a new form to see whether the answer changes. Trust gets replaced by an investigation that has no natural end.
article.development: Catching the next lie will not repair the first one. If the answer keeps changing, the terms may need to change with it. If the answer is honest, another round of private testing only creates a new reason to guard every word. Either way, control cannot do the work that trust was supposed to do.
article.close: Before {{exitDate}}, a broken agreement that never received an honest explanation may no longer deserve another investigation.
try_this: We can write down what was said separately from what we suspect it means.
We can say what we already know instead of waiting to see whether someone admits it.
We can change the terms when the same answer keeps changing.

article.opening: Mars enters Capricorn on {{entryDate}}, and the unfinished work stops looking impossible. The hard part gets done first. A vague goal becomes a deadline, a sequence, and visible proof that effort is leading somewhere. Progress replaces the argument about whether anyone feels ready.
article.tension: Then the standard moves. A finished step gets one more improvement, then another. Breaks start to look like weakness. Waiting on someone else feels inefficient, so we take their part too. The goal keeps moving forward while the work required to call it finished keeps getting larger.
article.development: Mars in Capricorn can keep going long after the original need has been met. Discipline loses its value when nothing is allowed to be enough. The effort stops leading anywhere and becomes punishment for not being finished enough. Ambition built this way can reach the deadline and leave nobody able to enjoy what was completed.
article.close: Before {{exitDate}}, the version that does the job may be worth more than the perfect version that takes everything with it.
try_this: We can compare the current work with the first definition of finished.
We can leave one optional improvement for later.
We can return one responsibility that was taken over only because waiting felt inefficient.

articles.engineRenderedFactLine: Saturn moves through all twelve signs in about twenty-nine years and usually spends roughly two and a half to three years in each sign.

article.opening: Saturn enters Aries on {{entryDate}}, and every delay begins to feel like a failure of nerve. A decision sits untouched until waiting becomes unbearable. Then it comes out as a declaration, and a choice that needed courage now has to be defended like a fight.
article.tension: Saturn slows what Aries wants to begin immediately. We can agree for too long, refuse too sharply, and call the final explosion honesty. A question sounds like resistance. An offer of help sounds like doubt. Independence becomes harder to carry because every choice has to prove that nobody else was needed.
article.development: Courage lasts longer when it does not have to prove itself through force. A limit said early stays a limit instead of turning into punishment. A first step can be small without being weak. Support does not erase independence; refusing every form of it can turn independence into another burden carried alone.
article.close: By {{exitDate}}, self-direction built on constant combat may feel less like freedom and more like another position that can never be put down.
try_this: We can say one no plainly the first time, instead of agreeing now and refusing sharply later.
We can make the smallest useful start on something delayed and let that start be enough for today.
We can accept one concrete offer of help without taking the task back midway.

articles.engineRenderedFactLine: Jupiter moves through all twelve signs in about twelve years and usually spends about one year in each sign.

article.opening: Jupiter enters Leo on {{entryDate}}, and the work we kept private becomes easier to show. Someone posts the first piece, accepts the invitation, or puts their name on an idea that used to be described as a group effort. Visibility brings confidence. Confidence makes the next version larger.
article.tension: Jupiter in Leo grows through creative courage and the willingness to be seen. The applause feels good because it confirms that the risk reached someone. Then the response becomes the measure. We promise more before the current work is finished, repeat the part that got noticed, and quietly drop what mattered when nobody praised it. Recognition starts deciding what deserves to exist.
article.development: The work can grow without being shaped around the reaction. A larger audience does not make every larger promise worth keeping. Praise can show what connected without deciding what gets made next. Once attention becomes the only proof, the work begins to lose the person who wanted to make it.
article.close: Before {{exitDate}}, work made only to hold attention may be harder to recognize as our own.
try_this: We can show one finished piece before promising the next one.
We can keep one unusual part even when the familiar part gets more praise.
We can name what we want to make before reading the response.
